summary: Creating the app is quick, but LinkedIn gates API surface behind 'products' you must request on the app's Products tab. Sign In with LinkedIn is self-serve; marketing and talent products involve applications and review.

approval.typical_timeline: App creation: minutes. Self-serve products: minutes. Reviewed products (e.g. Marketing Developer Platform): application + review, timeline not stated in fetched sources.
approval.notes: The app must be associated with a LinkedIn Page and verified before products can be used.

steps.title: Create an app in the LinkedIn developer portal
steps.detail: Apps are tied to a LinkedIn Page; you need to verify that association.

steps.title: Request products on the Products tab
steps.detail: Each product unlocks scopes/APIs. Open member permissions such as profile and email are available through the self-serve Sign In product.

steps.title: Choose the right flow: 3-legged vs 2-legged
steps.detail: Member Authorization (3-legged) is for acting on a member's behalf and is the common case; Application Authorization (2-legged client credentials) covers non-member-specific resources and is not supported by all APIs.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect the member, exchange the code, and request only the minimal scopes for your use case.

nuances: Not every API supports 2-legged OAuth; Marketing APIs require member authorization.
Requesting more products than you need slows approval and violates minimum-permission guidance.
agent_can_do: Match your feature list to the right LinkedIn products and flows
Flag which scopes need reviewed products before you promise a launch date
human_must_do: Create the app and verify the LinkedIn Page association
Represent your company accurately in review answers
